Cypress Springs Elementary enrolls 405 students in 2025-26 school year
G. A. Mcgill
Cypress Springs Elementary School had 405 students in the 2025-26 school year, according to the Louisiana Department of Education.
That figure was 12.5% higher than the previous school year, when enrollment stood at 360 students.
Of students enrolled in the 2025-26 school year, 55.1% were boys and 44.9% were girls.
Most students were Black, comprising 67.2% of Cypress Springs Elementary School's total enrollment.
The school is in the Lincoln Parish School District, whose central office is in Ruston.
Statewide, 660,349 students were enrolled in Louisiana in the 2025-26 school year.
Louisiana ranked near the bottom nationally for public school systems, according to WalletHub's 2026 analysis. The state ranked 44th among the 50 states and Washington, D.C., with a quality rank of 42 and a safety rank of 48. WalletHub compared states across 32 metrics, including student performance, funding, school safety, class size and instructor credentials.
Black and White students were the two largest groups reported in Louisiana public schools in 2025, according to KIDS COUNT data from Agenda for Children based on Louisiana Department of Education enrollment figures. Black students made up 41.8% of public school enrollment, while White students accounted for 40.2%. Hispanic students made up 11.6% of enrollment, continuing a long-term increase in the state's public schools.
Information in this article was obtained from the Kentucky Department of Education. The source data can be found here.
